name: kironi
trademark_risk: No live trademark for the exact string "KIRONI" surfaced in USPTO, EUIPO, UKIPO or WIPO results — searches for "kironi trademark" return only near-neighbours, and search engines aggressively autocorrect the query to "kiron", which is itself a signal that KIRONI is unregistered. The real exposure is the KIRON cluster one letter away: KIRON, Inc. (US, medical/analgesic goods — unrelated class, low risk), KIRON (SARL) (France), and most importantly Kiron Open Higher Education (kiron.ngo), a German-based education nonprofit operating "Kiron Campus", an online-learning platform and app. A German/EU education brand sitting one vowel from your name, in your exact sector, is the single biggest legal-and-confusion hazard here: an EUIPO class 9/41 opposition from Kiron is a plausible outcome, since KIRON vs KIRONI are visually and aurally near-identical for identical services. Also live: KIRONI LTD, a UK company incorporated 29 Dec 2025 (SIC 47910, internet retail) — a company registration, not a trademark, so it confers no blocking rights over class 9/41/42, but it does mean someone else is already trading under the exact word in the UK and may file. Recommendation: a proper knockout search on EUIPO/UKIPO for KIRON* in classes 9, 41, 42 before spending on branding.
appstore_play_risk: No app named exactly "Kironi" found on either the App Store or Google Play. However the confusion neighbourhood is dense and, unhelpfully, concentrated in education: "Kiron Campus - Online Learning" (Google Play, app.kironcampus) is a free online-learning app for refugees and asylum seekers — same category, near-identical name; "Kiron Performance" (deportnet.apps.kironperformance) is a fitness/nutrition app, which brushes your wellness pillar; "Kiron" is also a project-management app at kironapp.com, brushing your productivity pillar; plus "Kiro" (bio.kiro.app) and "Kirani" (App Store id6450255414). Practically this means App Store and Play search for "kironi" will surface Kiron Campus and Kiro alongside you, and ASO for the name will be a permanent uphill fight rather than a clean-slate win. No popular identical app exists, so this is not fatal, but the name buys you none of the discoverability advantage an invented name is supposed to deliver.
linguistic_issues: One genuine negative meaning, and it is not obscure: in Finnish, "kiro" means curse/swear-word, and "kironi" is its regular first-person possessive form — literally "my curse". Finnish speakers will read the brand as "my curse", which for a wellness and self-improvement app is an unfortunate inversion of the entire value proposition. Finland is a small market, but it is a high-ARPU Nordic one, and Duolingo/Finch-class ambitions imply eventually shipping there. "Kiro-" also carries the swearing connotation (kirosana = swear word), so the association is coarse as well as negative. Elsewhere the name is clean: nothing negative found in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian, Mandarin pinyin or Indonesian. Japanese parses it harmlessly as kiro-ni (帰路に "on the way home" / 岐路に "at a crossroads") — arguably a mild positive for a learning app. Pronunciation is easy and stable across languages (ki-ROH-nee, three open syllables, no consonant clusters), but the spelling is not self-evident from hearing it: expect chronic misspelling as "Kironni", "Kyroni", "Kironie", and above all "Kiron", which lands users straight on the education competitor described above. Homophone/typo leakage to KIRON is the practical linguistic problem, more than the Finnish meaning.
social_handles: No prominent brand or creator occupying "kironi" surfaced on X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or GitHub — searches return only unrelated near-matches such as GitHub user "kiryano". There is no established account with meaningful following on this handle, so exact-match handles are plausibly obtainable across the major platforms, though this should be verified by direct lookup on each platform rather than via search engines, which are unreliable for handle-squatting checks (dormant squatted handles do not rank). This is the strongest dimension of the name.
web_usage: Uncrowded as an exact string, which is the main thing the name has going for it. As a surname, Kironi is vanishingly rare — Forebears ranks it 4,649,889th worldwide at roughly 1 in 405 million people, concentrated in Indonesia (83% of bearers in Asia, 61% in Southeast Asia), with Hindi/Marathi/Oriya script renderings. It is not a notable place name and not a common given name; the only "name meaning" hits are algorithmic numerology filler sites, which is exactly the fingerprint of a word with no real cultural footprint. The crowding problem is entirely at one remove: KIRON is genuinely busy (Kiron Interactive, a South African virtual-sports gaming software firm; Kirona, a UK workforce-management SaaS; Kiron Corporation; Kyron, an enterprise startup launchpad; Kirin, both the Japanese beverage giant and a Solana crypto wallet on Google Play). No crypto token or funded startup was found operating as "Kironi" itself. Domain kironi.com appears registered/parked rather than actively developed — no live site surfaced — so acquisition cost is an open question worth checking via WHOIS before committing.
summary: MODERATE_RISK — usable, but it is not the clean invented name it looks like, and two specific problems should be weighed before committing. First, the trademark and app-store neighbourhood: no live KIRONI mark was found in any register, but KIRON is occupied in your exact sector by Kiron Open Higher Education (a German/EU online-learning nonprofit shipping "Kiron Campus" on Google Play), plus a Kiron fitness app and a Kiron project-management app that touch your wellness and productivity pillars respectively. KIRON versus KIRONI for identical class 9/41 services is close enough that an EUIPO opposition is a live possibility, and in the meantime store search will surface Kiron Campus next to you forever. Second, Finnish: "kironi" is the ordinary possessive of "kiro" (curse/swear word) and reads as "my curse" — a meaning that lands badly for a wellness app and rules out clean Nordic expansion without explanation. Against that, the positives are real: essentially zero web crowding on the exact string, a vanishingly rare surname (1 in ~405M, mostly Indonesian), no exact-match app anywhere, no company or token trading as Kironi in software, no offensive meaning in any of the other twelve languages checked, easy three-syllable pronunciation, and social handles that look obtainable across X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and GitHub. Nothing here is fatal and nothing rises to a live software trademark or an established same-space company using the exact name, which is why this lands mid-scale rather than HIGH_RISK. Before spending on branding I would do three things: a professional knockout search for KIRON* in classes 9, 41 and 42 at EUIPO and UKIPO, a direct platform-by-platform handle check (search engines do not reveal dormant squatted handles), and a WHOIS on kironi.com, which appears registered or parked with no live site. If the EUIPO search shows Kiron holding education-class marks, this name should be downgraded to HIGH_RISK and probably dropped.

name: lumiri
trademark_risk: No live US or EU trademark found for the exact string LUMIRI in Nice classes 9/41/42 (software, education, SaaS) — the class most relevant to you appears open. One exact-match USPTO filing exists: LUMIRI, serial 88929651, filed 2020-05-22 by Lumiri Surgical LLC (Lanham/Fort Washington, MD) for medical/surgical services (class 44 territory). Different class, low direct blocking risk for an app, but it establishes a senior US user of the identical word and would surface in any clearance search. Justia/USPTO detail pages returned 403 to automated fetch, so status (registered vs. abandoned) should be confirmed manually in TSDR before filing. Bigger latent hazard is the phonetic neighborhood: LUMII is a registered USPTO mark (serial 88867099) owned by Hangzhou Inshot Tech — the publisher of a very large consumer photo app — and LUMIRA, LUMIRE, LUMIR, LUMINARY are all registered or applied-for in adjacent consumer/software classes. A "LUMIRI" class 9/42 application is a realistic candidate for an office action or opposition on likelihood of confusion with LUMII/LUMIRA. Not fatal, but budget for a real attorney clearance search, not a knockout.
appstore_play_risk: No app named exactly "Lumiri" found on either the App Store or Google Play. The name is effectively free on both stores today. However the store shelf around it is crowded with near-identical strings that will hurt search discoverability and could draw a store name-dispute complaint: Lumii (Inshot's AI photo editor, one of the largest names in the category, plus a separate Lumii beauty/skincare-routine app), Lumirri (Avidz LLC, iOS), Lumire (two separate apps, iOS + Play), LUMIR (Lumir Inc. smart lighting), LUMIRISE, Lumier, and Lumiere: Anxiety & Stress Aid — the last of which is a wellness app by Fabulous, i.e. directly in your Finch/wellness lane. Expect "lumiri" queries to autocorrect toward Lumii/Lumiere in store search.
linguistic_issues: No offensive, vulgar, or negative meaning found in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin pinyin, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian, or Indonesian. Semantics are actively favorable: it reads as a coinage off Latin lumen / French lumière / Italian lumi ("lights") / Esperanto lumi ("to shine"), and Finnish lumi ("snow"). It registers as a rare given name in name databases (not in US SSA records). Pronunciation is easy across languages (loo-MEE-ree), three open syllables, no consonant clusters. The real linguistic weakness is spelling, not meaning: it is a poor radio test. Spoken aloud, "lumiri" is near-indistinguishable from Lumiri/Lumeri/Lumiree/Lumire/Lumiry and is one phoneme from Lumira, Lumari, Lumii, and Lumière — users will mistype it, and organic search will leak to bigger neighbors.
social_handles: No dominant single owner of @lumiri surfaced on X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or GitHub — no notable creator or brand account with meaningful following appeared in searches, so handles are plausibly obtainable or at worst squatted-but-dormant. Offsetting this: at least three commercial entities are already marketing under the exact name and will be competing for the same handles and hashtag — Lumiri Surgical (Facebook presence via Dr. Tiffany Schatz), the Lumiri Korean-botanicals skincare DTC brand at trylumiri.com, and a second Lumiri hair-coverage cream brand at lumiri.co. Verify each handle manually; treat availability as unconfirmed rather than clear.
web_usage: Moderately crowded, and the exact-match .com is gone. lumiri.com resolves to Lumiri Surgical / Dr. Tiffany Schatz MD, FACS (an active minimally-invasive surgery practice affiliated with Grand View Health, with an NPI record and a patient-facing site) — you will not get lumiri.com without a purchase negotiation, and you would be sharing top-of-search results with a medical practice. lumiri.co and lumiri.in are also both occupied by unrelated businesses, and trylumiri.com is an active e-commerce skincare brand, which is a telling signal: someone else already had to settle for a "try-" prefix. "Lumiri" is not a common surname, given name, or place name, so there is little generic noise, but the broader lum-/lumi- prefix is one of the most saturated zones in current consumer tech and wellness branding (Lumi, Lumii, Lumira, Lumari (YC), Luminai, Luminary, Lumino, Lumen, Lumira/SAP BusinessObjects Lumira), which compresses your SEO ceiling and makes the name feel derivative rather than ownable.
summary: MODERATE_RISK — usable, but not clean, and not cheap to own. Nothing here is disqualifying: no famous mark, no popular identical app, no offensive meaning in any of the thirteen languages checked, and no live software trademark on the exact string in classes 9/41/42. The problems are commercial rather than legal. First, lumiri.com is taken by an active US surgical practice that also holds an exact-match USPTO filing (serial 88929651, 2020) — different Nice class, so it likely will not block your registration, but it costs you the canonical domain and permanently splits your branded search results. Two more live consumer brands (a skincare DTC at trylumiri.com, a hair-cream brand at lumiri.co) are already using the exact name, which is why the .co and try- variants are gone too. Second, the phonetic neighborhood is genuinely hostile for a consumer app: LUMII is a registered mark held by a major app publisher, Lumiere is an existing wellness app, and Lumira/Lumari/Lumire/Lumirri all exist in adjacent consumer and software classes. Expect a real chance of a likelihood-of-confusion office action on a class 9/42 filing, and expect store-search and SEO leakage to bigger lum- neighbors from day one. If you proceed: commission an attorney knockout search before filing, confirm the Lumiri Surgical mark's current TSDR status, price lumiri.com early, and lock the social handles immediately. If the goal is a Finch/Duolingo-scale brand you actually own outright, the crowding alone is a reasonable argument for picking something further from the lumi- root.

name: manulo
trademark_risk: No live exact-match "MANULO" trademark surfaced in USPTO, EUIPO, or WIPO-fed sources. Justia/Trademarkia/USPTO searches return only phonetic neighbors, none in software classes: MANULOOT (Ser. 98119326), MANQO, MANO, MANU, MANANALU. Nearest corporate mark is MANULOC (French forklift-fleet maintenance group, Nice classes ~7/37/39 — industrial, not software), which is a distinct word plus a hard "c" and unlikely to block a Class 9/41/42 filing, though an EU examiner or opponent could raise similarity for a bare-word mark. Caveat: tmsearch.uspto.gov and euipo.europa.eu are JS-gated and returned 403 to direct fetch, so this is search-index evidence, not a certified clearance search — a paid knock-out search in classes 9/41/42 (US + EU + UK) is still required before filing. Also note MANULIFE (famous financial-services mark, global) shares the "MANU-" prefix; not a conflict for an unrelated app, but avoid any finance/insurance feature framing under this name.
appstore_play_risk: No app named "Manulo" found on the App Store or Google Play. Searches returned only "Manolo Technologies" (an unrelated Play developer) and noise from Manchester United / Manganelo. No popular or even minor identical-name app identified. The main store-search hazard is ambiguity rather than conflict: "manulo" collides in autocomplete and fuzzy search with the far more common "Manolo," and with Manchester United ("Man U") queries, so organic ASO discovery will be diluted. No blocking conflict.
linguistic_issues: The one genuinely adverse finding. Urban Dictionary carries an entry defining "Manulo" as "Derogatory for Mexican or Latin american" (posted 2009 by xequinoxed). Credibility is low — 0 upvotes / 0 downvotes, a single unvalidated 17-year-old submission, no corroboration in any dictionary, corpus, or slur database, and almost certainly a mangling of the Spanish name "Manolo." But it is currently the #1 result for "manulo meaning slang," which is exactly what a journalist or a hostile poster would find. Treat as reputational, not linguistic, risk. Otherwise clean: no meaning found in French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin pinyin, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian, or Indonesian. In Spanish it reads as a near-miss for "Manolo" (common diminutive of Manuel) and shares the "mano" (hand) root, which is benign-to-warm. In Esperanto it parses as mano + -ulo = roughly "hand-person," harmless. Pronunciation is easy and near-universal (ma-NOO-lo, three open syllables, no consonant clusters, no phonemes absent from major languages). Spelling risk is the real cost: users will hear it and type "Manolo" — the dominant homophone by a wide margin.
social_handles: Not heavily crowded but not free. Instagram has @manulo_cz and @_manulo (~595 followers, 33 posts) — the underscore variants strongly imply bare @manulo is already registered. TikTok has @d.manulo (small creator). There is an active music artist "Manulo" on Apple Music (artist ID 751960307) and SoundCloud (@manuloofficial). A Polish company runs Facebook page @panelmanulo. No GitHub org conflict surfaced. Expect to need suffixed handles (@manuloapp, @getmanulo) across most platforms — normal for a short invented name, but it means no clean handle set.
web_usage: Moderately crowded, and the most material finding sits here: manulo.pl is an active Polish consumer digital brand — "Panel Badawczy Manulo," a paid online survey / market-research panel operated out of Opole, with ESOMAR/PKJPA accreditation, a Facebook presence, third-party review coverage, and a consumer signup funnel. Exact name match, consumer-facing, digital, EU, and it pays users for completing tasks — adjacent enough to a rewards-driven productivity/wellness app to create real confusion in EU markets and to give them arguable prior common-law rights in Poland. It appears to be a small operator, not a funded startup. Separately, manulo.com is not available: it 302-redirects to atom.com/name/Manulo, i.e. it is inventory on a brandable-domain marketplace, so expect a four-to-five-figure acquisition cost or a compromise TLD. "Manulo" is not a documented surname, given name, or place name; general web volume is otherwise low, dominated by MANULOC (French industrial services) and by misspelling traffic for Manolo.
summary: MODERATE_RISK — usable, but it carries three unglamorous costs and one small landmine. No fatal conflict exists: no live software trademark in classes 9/41/42, no app of this name on either store, no funded company, no famous mark, and no offensive meaning in any real language. What blocks a CLEAR grade is (1) manulo.pl, an active exact-name Polish consumer research-panel brand that pays users for tasks — same name, same continent, adjacent-enough space to muddy EU launch and to assert local prior use; (2) manulo.com is held on a brandable-domain marketplace, so the .com is a purchase, not a registration; (3) bare @manulo appears taken across Instagram, with an existing music artist on Apple Music and SoundCloud, so the handle set is compromised. The landmine is a zero-vote 2009 Urban Dictionary entry calling "Manulo" a derogatory term for Mexicans — almost certainly a corruption of "Manolo" and not a real slur, but it is the top result for "manulo meaning," which is a screenshot waiting to happen. The quieter strategic cost is the "Manolo" homophone: users will mishear and mistype it, permanently taxing word-of-mouth and app-store search. Recommended if you proceed: commission a real knock-out search in classes 9/41/42 across US/EU/UK before spending on identity, budget for the .com, and file early in the EU given the Polish incumbent. If a cleaner candidate exists in the shortlist, the .com cost plus the Manolo spelling drag are reasonable grounds to prefer it.

name: netimi
trademark_risk: No exact "NETIMI" mark surfaced in USPTO, EUIPO/UKIPO, or WIPO-adjacent sources — repeated searches returned only neighbors (NETIS, NETIX, NETIM, NETOMI), which is the expected signature of a genuinely unregistered coined term. The material concern is NETOMI: an established US AI-software company (formerly msg.ai, ~$217M raised, Fortune 500 enterprise CX customers) that is an active USPTO filer (e.g. Netomi, Inc. serial 98054238 for ANSWERSGPT) and almost certainly holds live class 9/42 registrations for AI software. NETIMI vs NETOMI differ by a single internal vowel; under sight/sound/commercial-impression analysis both would recite "downloadable software featuring artificial intelligence" in class 9, so a 2(d) citation on examination is a real possibility even though channels of trade differ (consumer self-improvement app vs enterprise customer-service platform). Secondary, weaker: NETIM (French ICANN-accredited registrar, likely EU class 42 rights — services-only, unlikely to reach a consumer app) and NETIS (85936385, networking hardware). Recommendation: this is not a self-clear; commission an attorney knockout search focused on the NETOMI family before filing.
appstore_play_risk: No app named "netimi" exists on either store. Nearest hits: "Netomi Agentic AI" on Google Play (com.netomi.sampleapplication — a low-install enterprise demo/sample app, not a consumer competitor), "Netim" (com.oristelekom.netim, small Turkish telecom app), "Nettime Kiosk", "Nettimoto" (Alma Media motorcycle marketplace, Finland), "Netmin", "Netti: Modern Network Tools", "My Netis". None are popular consumer apps and none occupy education/AI/productivity/wellness. Store-listing keyword collision is negligible; App Store name availability should be clean. The only naming-adjacency worth noting is that Netomi's presence means an ASO search for "netomi" could partially surface you and vice versa.
linguistic_issues: No offensive, vulgar, or negative meaning found in any of the checked languages. It is not a dictionary word in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin pinyin, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian, or Indonesian. Notes: (a) Turkish speakers will parse it as "net-im-i" — "net" is a live Turkish word meaning clear/net, giving a mildly positive "clarity" read rather than a problem; (b) Italian ears may hear it near "nettimi" (from netto, clean/clear) — again benign-to-positive; (c) it is phonotactically close to South Asian given names (Nethmi, Sinhala, "beautiful eyes") and the Indian surname Nettimi, so it reads as a personal name to some audiences; (d) Sanskrit "neti" (नेति, "not this / no end") is a faint but harmless resonance. Pronunciation is easy and near-unambiguous in most languages (neh-TEE-mee / NET-i-mee), all open CV syllables. Main friction is spelling-from-hearing: listeners may write netomi, netimy, nettimi, or netime, so you would want defensive domain and handle registrations on those variants.
social_handles: No established handle or brand presence under "netimi" was found on X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or GitHub — searches returned zero accounts using the string and instead surfaced unrelated content. Handle availability across the major platforms looks realistically obtainable, which is unusual and a point in the name's favor. The exposure is again on the neighbor side: @netomi is taken by the AI company across platforms, so verify you can secure exact-match handles rather than being pushed to a suffixed variant that increases confusion with them.
web_usage: The namespace is essentially empty — this is a genuinely coined string with near-zero organic web footprint. "netimi" is not a place name and not a standalone surname; the closest is Nettimi (double-t), an uncommon surname carried by roughly 244 people, mostly in India, with claimed Italian dialect roots. netimi.com returned HTTP 404 rather than an active business or a parked broker page, suggesting the domain may be unregistered or undeveloped — worth an immediate registrar check. Search engines aggressively autocorrect "netimi" toward "Netomi," which is the single biggest practical drawback: your SEO and word-of-mouth traffic will leak to a well-funded AI company for the first few years until you build enough signal to own the query.
summary: "netimi" is a clean coined name with no exact trademark, no app, no company, no crypto token, no social-handle squatter, and no bad meaning in any major language — an unusually empty namespace. It falls short of CLEAR for one reason: NETOMI, an established, well-funded AI-software company with active USPTO filings and a Play Store listing, is one vowel away and operates in the same broad class 9/42 AI-software territory. Search engines already autocorrect "netimi" to "Netomi," which is both a legal-confusion signal and an ongoing SEO tax. The goods/channels differ (consumer education-wellness app vs enterprise customer-service AI), so this is arguable rather than fatal, but it is exactly the kind of conflict that produces a 2(d) office action. Verdict MODERATE_RISK: usable, but do not file without an attorney knockout search against the NETOMI family, confirm netimi.com is actually available, and secure netomi-adjacent defensive spellings.

name: bonaka
trademark_risk: No live software/app trademark found. The exact word IS registered and commercially used, but only in hard goods: USPTO "BONAKA" Serial 77059136, filed 2006-12-07 by AMM GROUP, INC. d/b/a Bonaka USA, covering tool aprons, tool belts, tool holders and tool pouches (Class 18/22-type goods, not 9/41/42). Registry status could not be confirmed as LIVE via public search — the Justia/USPTO record surfaced but TSDR status was not retrievable, so this needs a paid/manual clearance check. No EUIPO, UKIPO, WIPO/Madrid record for "bonaka" surfaced in any class; searches returned only generic office pages, which is weak negative evidence rather than proof of clearance — run TMview and Madrid Monitor directly before filing. No famous mark is identical. The one adjacency worth noting: BONAQUA (ボナクア), Coca-Cola's global bottled-water brand, is phonetically close in Japanese/European markets and is a well-known mark in Class 32 — cross-class dilution risk is low for an app but it does erode distinctiveness. Classes 9/41/42 appear open for "bonaka" on the evidence available.
appstore_play_risk: No app named exactly "bonaka" exists on Google Play or the iOS App Store — searches surfaced only near-misses, and no popular incumbent. The meaningful conflict is one letter away: Banaka App Studio (banaka.in) is an active Google Play developer publishing knowledge/education apps (spirituality, Indian law, calendars, novels). Same broad category as your education+productivity positioning, and "Bonaka" vs "Banaka" is a single-vowel difference that store search algorithms and users will conflate — expect ASO cannibalization and a plausible (if not strong) confusion argument, particularly in the Indian market. Other near-names are unrelated and small: Bonata (POS, iOS), BonApp / BonApp Merchant (F&B), BoNOKi (Bluetooth locks), Bonako (games developer). None are famous, none are in your space, none are fatal.
linguistic_issues: No offensive meaning found in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian or Indonesian — the word reads as clean invented-Romance across all major app markets. Two minor blemishes. (1) Malagasy: Wiktionary lists "bonaka" as a real word meaning "swelling from disease," also dodder (a parasitic plant), and in the Betsileo dialect a fast-growing sweet potato; as an adjective, "round." Disease-swelling is an unfortunate gloss for a wellness app, though Malagasy is a negligible market. (2) Tagalog near-homophone: "bonak" is slang for stupid/idiot, a contraction of "bobong anak" ("stupid child") — Filipino users may hear "bonaka" as an inflected form of it. The Philippines is a large English-language app market, so this is worth a native-speaker gut check, but it is a near-miss rather than a direct hit. Pronunciation is easy and stable everywhere: bo-NA-ka, three open syllables, no consonant clusters, no ambiguous vowels, spells cleanly from hearing. Homophone risk is mainly against Banaka (see app stores) and, more loosely, Bonaqua.
social_handles: Not heavily contested. No dominant creator, brand, or repo owns "bonaka" on X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or GitHub — targeted searches surfaced nothing but generic noise, which for a coined word usually indicates low occupancy. The visible social footprint belongs to the Japanese trading company: Facebook pages "Bonaka - ボナカ" (facebook.com/bonakaofficial) and 株式会社ボナカジャパン (facebook.com/bonaka.co.jp), plus a Rakuten storefront. Treat exact-handle availability as unverified rather than confirmed — the search layer cannot enumerate platform handle registries, so check @bonaka manually on each platform. Realistic expectation: some are free, some squatted-but-dormant, and a @getbonaka / @bonakaapp fallback may be needed on one or two.
web_usage: Moderately crowded, but almost entirely outside tech. The dominant occupant is a real multinational commercial group: Bonaka Limited (Hong Kong), a large bags/luggage/outdoor-products manufacturer with a ~400,000 sq ft factory and 3,500+ workers; 株式会社ボナカジャパン / Bonaka Japan (bonaka.co.jp), a trading company founded 2002 making OEM tool bags — including the "ORCA TOOLBAG" for the Japan Air Self-Defense Force — and amusement-facility supplies; and Bonaka USA (AMM Group, Inc.), the US trademark holder and an H-1B visa sponsor. So the exact name is actively traded under in three countries, with bonaka.co.jp occupied and bonaka.com very likely held by the same group or parked — budget for a bonaka.app / getbonaka.com / trybonaka.com domain, not the clean .com. "Bonaka" is also a real surname, concentrated in DR Congo (most common country), with clusters in India and Nigeria. No startup, SaaS product, funded company, or crypto token with this name was found. No place name found. Net: the word is not a blank slate, but nothing occupying it competes with a consumer app.
summary: MODERATE_RISK — usable, but not the clean coined name it first appears to be. The good news is decisive on the fatal criteria: no famous mark, no popular identical app, no offensive meaning. Classes 9/41/42 look open, no software or app trademark exists anywhere I could reach, no app named "bonaka" ships on either store, and no startup, SaaS, or token holds the name. The drag is threefold. First, the word is already commercially occupied by an active three-country trading group — Bonaka Limited (HK), Bonaka Japan, and Bonaka USA, which holds a 2006 USPTO registration on tool belts and pouches. That is a different Nice class and no bar to your filing, but it means bonaka.co.jp is gone, bonaka.com is probably unavailable, the first page of Google belongs to tool bags, and a well-capitalized incumbent could make noise if you ever extend into physical goods or merch. Second, and more practically annoying: Banaka App Studio publishes education apps on Google Play, one vowel away from you, in your exact category. That is ASO collision and user confusion in the Indian market, not litigation, but it is the finding most likely to cost you real money. Third, minor linguistic static — Malagasy "bonaka" means swelling from disease (bad flavor for wellness, negligible market), and Tagalog "bonak" is slang for idiot, close enough that the Philippines deserves a native-speaker check. Phonetics are otherwise excellent: bo-NA-ka is three open syllables, spells from hearing, travels globally. Before committing, do three things: pull the real TSDR status on Serial 77059136, run TMview and Madrid Monitor directly rather than trusting search-surfaced results, and confirm @bonaka handle availability platform by platform. If those come back clean, this is a viable name that will cost you the .com and force a fight for search results against luggage.

appstore_play_risk: Clean. No crypto token, no SaaS product, no funded startup under this name. The app-store name field appears genuinely open in both stores, which is the single strongest point in this candidate's favor.
linguistic_issues: No offensive or vulgar meaning found in any of the checked languages (English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin pinyin, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Russian, Indonesian). summary: MODERATE_RISK — usable, but not a clean win. The good news is real: no live trademark for MEREPI in any jurisdiction I could surface, nothing in Nice classes 9/41/42, no existing app on either store, no company, SaaS, or token in the space, no offensive meaning in any of the 13 languages checked, and no established social handle-holder. social_handles: Contested, and this is the most concrete practical cost. name: naruke
trademark_risk: No live NARUKE trademark surfaced in USPTO/EUIPO/WIPO-indexed sources in any class, including 9/41/42 — searches on Justia/Trademarkia returned zero NARUKE marks (only NARUTO, NARUKO, NAROO). That is the good news. The real exposure is confusing similarity to NARUTO, a famous mark owned by Kabushiki Kaisha Shueisha with heavy live coverage in exactly our classes (Class 9 downloadable software/games and Class 41 entertainment/education) — e.g. Reg. 3229574 and Reg. 3280366. NARUKE differs from NARUTO by a single final letter, shares the first five characters, and would appear adjacent in app-store keyword and trademark-watch results. Shueisha and its licensees are known aggressive enforcers with active watch services; a Class 9/41 application for a consumer mobile app is a realistic candidate for an opposition or at minimum a demand letter. Sound-alike NARUKO (Taiwanese cosmetics) is live but Class 3 and non-conflicting. Note also Japanese-surname prior-use holders (Makoto Naruke, Michiko Naruke) — not registrations, but relevant to personal-name refusal grounds if any filing suggests a living individual. Recommend a professional clearance/watch opinion focused specifically on the NARUTO family before filing.
appstore_play_risk: No app named "naruke" found on Google Play or the iOS App Store. The nearest hit is "Naruka" (com.naruka), an obscure Indian mobile-dealer utility APK with negligible install base and no education/AI/wellness overlap — one-letter difference but effectively dormant. The material app-store problem is discovery, not collision: searching "naruke" in either store will be dominated by the enormous NARUTO franchise app catalog (games, streaming, wallpapers), so organic search for the brand will be swamped and fuzzy-matched to Naruto for years. App Store Connect name approval itself should pass; the risk is a Shueisha takedown request via the stores' IP complaint channels, which is cheap for them to file and disruptive to us.
linguistic_issues: No offensive or vulgar meaning found in any of the checked languages — this is the name's strongest attribute. Japanese: 成毛 / 鳴毛 (naruke) is a real, low-frequency surname; the kanji 鳴毛 reads roughly "crying hair," which is mildly odd but the romaji carries no connotation to Japanese speakers, who will simply hear a family name. It also sits inside the very productive naru- cluster (naru = "to become") so it feels natural and pronounceable in Japan. Russian/Ukrainian: "naruke" is a near-exact transliteration of "на руке" (na ruke) = "on the hand/arm" — harmless, arguably a pleasant accidental connotation for a habit/wellness app, but Slavic-language speakers will parse it as a prepositional phrase rather than a name. Serbo-Croatian similarly reads "na ruke" (to/into the hands). No adverse meaning in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Korean, Mandarin pinyin (not a valid syllable sequence — will be read letter-by-letter), Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, or Indonesian. Pronunciation is easy and unambiguous across languages (na-ROO-kay / NA-roo-keh), three open CV syllables. Two spelling hazards: the final -e is silent-e-prone for English speakers who may say "na-ROOK," and the dominant homophone/near-homophone problem is autocorrect and mishearing toward Naruto, which is the single most likely way a user types the wrong thing.
social_handles: Not heavily contested as a brand handle. No prominent X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or GitHub account operating under "naruke" surfaced in searches. Existing usage is individual and low-volume: Michiko Naruke, the Wild Arms video-game composer, has a modest presence including soundcloud.com/naruke-michiko and an NTS artist page, and Makoto Naruke (ex-president of Microsoft Japan, founder of Honz) is an active public figure with a Facebook presence under his own name. Expect to need suffixed handles (@narukeapp, @getnaruke) as a fallback, and expect hashtag noise from Naruto misspellings.
web_usage: Lightly crowded in absolute terms but poorly differentiated in practice. "Naruke" functions almost entirely as a Japanese surname: Makoto Naruke (Microsoft Japan president 1991-2000, prolific author, investor), Michiko Naruke (composer), and multiple patent inventors (Yasuo Naruke, Giichi Naruke) appear across Justia. There is one small US business, Naruke Bookkeeping — a Washington State payroll/bookkeeping shop serving Japanese-speaking small businesses, listed on ZoomInfo with a live comcastbiz site; it is a different class of service, tiny, and not a meaningful trademark obstacle, though it does hold the most brand-shaped prior use. No startup, funded company, SaaS product, or crypto token named Naruke was found. No place name of note. naruke.com could not be confirmed as available or parked from search alone and needs a direct WHOIS check before committing. Overall SEO verdict: the term itself is uncrowded and winnable, but every search will contend with Naruto-driven fuzzy matching, which is the dominant practical drag.
summary: MODERATE_RISK, sitting at the upper end of that band. Searching adversarially, I could not find the things that would kill this name: no live NARUKE trademark in any jurisdiction or class, no app of that name on either store, no startup, SaaS product, or token, and no offensive or embarrassing meaning in any of the thirteen languages checked. Pronunciation is clean and near-universal. The one substantive finding is proximity to NARUTO — a famous mark with dense live registrations in Classes 9 and 41, the exact classes a consumer education/AI/wellness app files in, owned by an owner with a documented enforcement posture. A single trailing letter separates them, which creates both a genuine opposition/takedown exposure and a permanent discoverability tax, since app-store and web search for "naruke" will be swamped by one of the largest media franchises on earth. Secondary, non-blocking noise: "naruke" is an established Japanese surname carried by two public figures, one tiny US bookkeeping firm holds the closest brand-shaped prior use, and Slavic speakers will read it as "на руке" (on the hand) — harmless, mildly charming for a wellness product. Recommendation: do not adopt without a professional clearance opinion scoped specifically to the NARUTO mark family, and confirm naruke.com ownership via direct WHOIS. If that opinion comes back clean and the domain is obtainable, the name is workable; if the client has low appetite for IP friction or depends on organic search, prefer a candidate that does not live one keystroke from a global franchise.

summary: BUKIRO is a genuinely uncontested string commercially — no trademark registration anywhere, no company, no SaaS, no crypto token, no app store listing, and no offensive or awkward meaning in any of the thirteen languages checked. It pronounces cleanly and universally. It is not CLEAR, however, for two reasons. First, it fully contains BUKI, which is a crowded live mark family including a Class 9 software registration (Loud-Hailer, Reg. 6125219) and, more worryingly, BUKI FRANCE's educational-products marks (Reg. 6126842 / IR 79259778) with EU and WIPO reach — an education-plus-AI app filing in Classes 9/41/42 has a real chance of an examiner citation or a watch-notice from BUKI France, so counsel should run a proper knockout before you invest in the mark. Second, the exact string is already spoken for in two small but visible places: the GitHub/Ko-fi handle "bukiro" belongs to an active Pathfinder RPG tool developer, and "Bukiro Football TV" runs on TikTok and YouTube; on top of that, Bukiro is a real Ugandan subcounty and peak plus a Tanzanian locality, which permanently occupies part of the SERP. None of that rises to a blocker — the geographic usage is non-commercial, the RPG tool is a different category, and the football channel is tiny — but you should expect to need a suffixed handle on GitHub and possibly elsewhere, and you should confirm @bukiro on X and Instagram manually since low-activity handles do not reliably surface in search. Net: a strong, distinctive, ownable candidate worth proceeding with, conditional on a professional trademark knockout clearing the BUKI family and on securing bukiro.com plus defensive registrations for Bukero/Bukiru.
